elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer (no covenant not to develop, market, sell or acquire competing products)
elements.evidence: 12.4 ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory") is deleted in the rendered clause.

elements.element: No field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer's business
elements.evidence: 12.3 retained: "Nothing restricts Customer from ... conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: No exclusivity/no-hire/minimum-volume commitment surviving as a de facto non-compete
elements.evidence: "Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment."

elements.element: Any restriction limited to a single named competing product
elements.evidence: Condition absent: no competing-activity restriction remains after deletion of 12.4.

elements.element: Restriction lasts during the term only
elements.evidence: The "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter" survival tail was removed with 12.4.
No duration remains; 24-month post-term period deleted.
12.3 preserves the right to develop "any product or service"; no restriction to carve out from.
12.3 preserves "developing, acquiring, licensing, selling" any product or service.

reasons: The locked preferred level is fully achieved: the only operative restriction on Customer (12.4) is removed, and 12.3's affirmative no-non-compete acknowledgement is left intact.

Deleting the whole of 12.4 is the narrowest available edit because the entire paragraph is the offending covenant — it contains no unrelated commercial term, trigger or mechanic worth preserving, so no operator, number or short-phrase change could deliver the preferred position. The deterministic minimality gate's generic 'whole paragraph' objection does not apply on these facts.

Fallback constraints (named product, term-only, 12-month cap, development/acquisition carve-outs) are vacuously satisfied because the conditioning restriction is demonstrably absent; no fallback element has been imported into the preferred outcome.
Intent is preserved: no cross-reference depended on 12.4, no defined term is orphaned, and the deletion resolves the direct contradiction with 12.3.
